card.what: 70 mm stainless snap shackle with a fixed eye: a hinged bail that snaps shut on a spring plunger and opens under load with a pull ring
card.boats: J/22 spinnaker sheets, guys and halyard (clipped to the kite's clews and head); later the Catalina 22's jib halyard
card.distance: arm's reach: in the hand on the foredeck and at the shrouds, and in close-ups of the spinnaker hoist and drop
card.before: nothing in the kit: the nearest part is ShackleD, the 5 mm D-shackle with a screw pin, so the sheet shows that as the stand-in

references.use: outline and proportions (near square-on side view: fixed eye, bail, latch boss, plunger ring); measuring only

references.url: Wichard 2472 (fixed eye, 70 mm) retailer listings: Jimmy Green, Blue Marine Store, CE Marine (numbers only)
references.note: length 70 mm, A 21 mm, B 13 mm, 90 g, working load 1280 kg; Wichard 2473 swivel eye 70 mm is 65 g. The listings don't say what A and B measure: on the photo the bail's inside width is about 21 mm and the eye's about 15 mm

Width across, pull ring to bail
sizes.source: reported only: the ring hangs where it falls

features.text: Fixed oval eye forged into the body, big enough for a spliced sheet
One forged body: a diagonal crossbar and a plunger column, soft fillets, no seams
Hinged bail of round bar arcing over the top from the hinge to the latch
Hinge: the bail's fork round a knuckle on a cross pin with heads
Round latch boss at the top of the column where the bail's tip seats
Plunger lug out of the column with a pull ring (about 12 mm) to open it
Bail opening about 21 mm across: room for a clew ring or a sail's head
Maker's mark on the crossbar's face (made up, no real logo)

budget.note: hero is a Nanite part; build_kit makes the light copy at a quarter of the triangles
